evidence_checks.located_span: Since they're made out of PU I'm wondering if the material ever starts peeling, especially since a work bag would be something for daily use.
evidence_checks.note: Worry or question rather than a firm expectation; it also cites reviews of Beis peeling. Weak support.

evidence_checks.located_span: the Beis complaints about peeling is going to happen to any
evidence_checks.note: Expects any vegan leather bag to peel.

evidence_checks.located_span: Anything which is just PU leather will start peeling with daily use.
evidence_checks.note: Direct statement that PU peels with daily use.

scope_issue: The text says about 4.5 years where the claim says about four. The claim leaves out two other positive owner reports in the contradicting set (Poppy and Peonies, Matt and Nat), so 'one owner' understates the counter-evidence. Nothing in the sources is about the Lévant material.
reasoning: Several commenters across three threads say PU or vegan leather will peel or fail to hold up, and E-0415 is an owner report of a microfiber bag with no cracking after about 4.5 years. The claim describes beliefs, so the positive owner reports in the contradicting set do not falsify it, although they show the single counterexample is not the only one. One supporting source is about jackets and one is a question rather than an expectation, but the pattern of beliefs is still adequately supported.

evidence_checks.located_span: I bought a vegan leather bomber only because I was able to Get it for super cheap on sale. I would never pay full price or over $70 for vegan leather. All my faux leather jackets start flaking and peeling after a few years.
evidence_checks.note: Purchase motive (cheap on sale) is stated outright. The commenter's peeling experience is stated, but the text does not say the bomber purchase came after it; the sequence is inferred.

evidence_checks.located_span: Freja Paloma (too pricey for vegan leather
evidence_checks.note: Shopper excluded the Freja Paloma as too pricey for vegan leather; peeling is not given as the reason, consistent with the claim.

scope_issue: The phrase 'after vegan leather had peeled for them' infers a sequence the text does not state outright; the text gives general past peeling of faux leather jackets alongside the cheap-only purchase.
reasoning: Both individual decisions are stated in the sources: one person bought a vegan leather bomber only because it was cheap on sale, and their faux leather jackets have peeled; another excluded a tote as too pricey for vegan leather. The timing link between the peeling and the purchase is a mild inference, not a stated sequence. E-0417 (someone who bought a Harlow) does not contradict either individual account.

scope_issue: The sources are self-selected complaint threads; several owners in the same threads report 5-7 years of use without major failure, which the claim does not mention but does not deny. The sources are about backpacks, not the Lévant tote.
reasoning: Failure reports come from three distinct threads and cover zippers, straps and fabric. The stated timings run from under a month (E-0078) to just after two years (E-0103), which matches the claim's range. The contradicting long-life reports show failures are not universal, but the claim only says these owners report failures, so they do not contradict it.

scope_issue: Some intentions are implied rather than stated (E-0041, E-0050, E-0060, E-0094), and E-0019 is second-hand; the claim's caveat covers this. None are verified non-purchases.
reasoning: Nine comments tie a decision not to buy, or to hold off, to negative reviews or to the brand's Reddit replies. The reply-driven ones (E-0019, E-0020, E-0026, E-0060, E-0062) are indeed in two threads, 18nj9sk and bqe83z. The claim correctly frames these as stated intentions. The contradicting repeat-buyer reports describe other people and do not negate these accounts.

evidence_checks.located_span: they responded that either give me 30% money back or I pay for the return cost.
evidence_checks.note: Partial refund offered as the alternative to a return at the buyer's cost. However, the same post says 'The return address is a port in Commerce, CA.', not Hong Kong; 'HONG KONG SELLER' describes the seller, not the return destination.

evidence_checks.located_span: the address you have to ship it back to is in Hong Kong. I wanted to return a backpack and a couple of other items and it would have cost me almost as much as the backpack itself. They offered a 30% refund to me but only gave me 21%.
evidence_checks.note: Hong Kong return at high buyer cost, and a partial refund offered. Fully matches the claim.

scope_issue: The 'return to Hong Kong' detail holds for only one of the two buyers; the other was told to return to Commerce, CA. Neither source explicitly says a free return was refused, though E-0036 implies it.
reasoning: Both buyers describe being offered a partial (30%) refund rather than a return at Nordace's expense. Only E-0074 says the return address was in Hong Kong; E-0036 gives a California address, so 'two buyers ... return to Hong Kong' overstates the evidence. E-0092 concerns a free warranty replacement, a different situation, and does not contradict these accounts.

evidence_checks.note: Heavy retargeting stated directly as the cause of suspicion.

evidence_checks.located_span: I was considering buying one after seeing an ad, but it seemed a little... suspicious.

scope_issue: Only two commenters clearly cite these reasons for suspicion (E-0002 countdown reset, E-0040 retargeting); 'a few' stretches the evidence, since E-0050 does not cite retargeting and E-0093 expresses annoyance, not suspicion.
reasoning: E-0002 and E-0040 directly support the claim: a sale timer that reset undermined one buyer's trust, and aggressive ad tailing made another suspicious. E-0050 is suspicion after an ad without reference to retargeting, and E-0093 is irritation rather than suspicion, so the count behind 'a few' is thin. E-0083 is a satisfied buyer and does not contradict these individual accounts.
